title: Terra preta (Amazonian dark earths) near Manaus
summary: Terra preta is rich, dark soil left behind by ancient Amazonians. Archaeologists working near Manaus, at the meeting of the Negro and Solimões rivers, report deposits dating back about 2,000 years, and one says it appeared in almost every part of the Amazon Basin by A.D. 500 to 1000. Patches typically cover 1 to 5 hectares.

uncertainty.note: Sources give ages relative to their publication, not calendar years: Science (2002) says the oldest deposits "date back more than 2000 years"; Harvard says "nearly 2,000 years ago". The window here is an approximation of those phrases, not a sourced calendar date.
